title: Your Shares Just Hit a 'Pause Button': Understanding Stock Market Circuit Breakers
description: Circuit breakers are safety mechanisms in the stock market that temporarily stop trading. There are two main types: "price bands" for individual stocks and "m.

faq.a: An upper circuit is the highest price an individual stock is allowed to trade at on a given day, set as a percentage above its previous closing price.
A lower circuit is the lowest price an individual stock is allowed to trade at on a given day, set as a percentage below its previous closing price.

faq.q: How often do market-wide circuit breakers get triggered?
faq.a: Market-wide circuit breakers are very rare. They have only been triggered a few times in India's history, typically during major events causing extreme market stress, such as the global financial crisis in 2008 or the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

faq.q: Can I still place orders when a circuit is hit?
faq.a: Generally, no new orders can be placed for a stock once it hits its circuit limit until trading resumes or the next trading day. For market-wide halts, all trading across equity and derivatives segments stops.

faq.q: Do circuit breakers apply to all stocks?
faq.a: Stock-specific price bands apply to most individual stocks, but the percentage limits can vary. Market-wide circuit breakers apply to the entire equity and equity derivatives market if the benchmark indices cross their thresholds.
